title: RBAC v2 migration: disable legacy RBAC v1 checks for initial endpoint set (post-shadow)
author: Benji Okafor
description: Context: We have been running RBAC v2 in dual-eval (v1 enforced, v2 evaluated + shadow-deny metrics) since PR #18579. Shadow-deny rate for the endpoints listed below has been ~0 for 10 days in staging and 6 days in hosted canary, and we have verified support/break-glass flows are not hitting these routes. This PR removes/disables the legacy RBAC v1 checks for the first tranche of control-plane endpoints, leaving RBAC v2 as the single source of truth for authorization decisions (still behind the existing enforcement feature flag). Scope: Included endpoints (initial tranche): (1) API key management: create/rotate/revoke/list (org + project scopes) (2) Org membership read/list + role assignment read (write remains gated by flag) (3) Billing read-only surfaces used by console to render invoices/usage summaries (no payment method updates yet) (4) Model rollout read/list endpoints used by console dashboards (no rollout mutation yet). Not included (explicitly out of scope in this PR): SSO/SAML configuration endpoints, audit log export endpoints, Dedicated autoscaling/GPU pool admin endpoints, Private installer/admin flows, and any data-plane/inference hot-path operations. Implementation notes: (a) Delete the v1 middleware hooks on the above routes and route everything through the v2 Authorize() call (b) Retain the v1 codepath behind an emergency env override (RBAC_V1_FALLBACK_ENABLED) but do not execute by default (c) Keep the shadow metrics emitted for v2 decisions (allow/deny counters + reason codes) to maintain parity with dashboards (d) Update integration tests to assert v1 is not called (mock expectation) and that v2 deny reasons are stable. Rollout plan: no behavior change for customers until rbacv2.enforce=true (existing flag). After merge, we will run in hosted canary with rbacv2.enforce=true AND legacy v1 disabled for 24h before expanding to 25% / 100% per the rollout playbook. Rollback plan (documented below) is flag-first; code revert is the last resort. Checklist: - [x] Confirm shadow-deny metrics <= 0.1% for included routes - [x] Validate support tooling does not depend on these routes with v1-only grants - [x] Update tests + add a guard to prevent re-introducing v1 checks on migrated routes - [x] Add release note for internal ops (on-call) re: rollback switches. References: ENG-5389 (migration), PR #18579 (dual-eval), PR #18480 (API key RBAC v2 checks), PR #18451 (403 reason codes/logging).
commits: rbac(migration): introduce route allowlist for v1-disable tranche
rbac(control-plane): remove legacy v1 middleware from api-keys + billing read routes
tests(authz): assert v1 evaluator not invoked on migrated endpoints
ops: document rollback switches and add runbook link in service README
conversation: Kaitlyn Nguyen (review): Please confirm that disabling v1 here doesn’t remove the audit logging context we added in #18522 (actor/role/policy_version). Also, the tranche list includes org role assignment read—do we have any console routes that still assume v1 errors? Benji Okafor (author): Audit logging is unaffected; it’s emitted from the v2 middleware after policy evaluation. Added a regression test that asserts authz fields are present on deny for /orgs/{id}/api-keys. For console, this PR only touches membership read + role assignment read; the UI can already render v2 403 reason codes since #18451. Jordan Lee (review): I’m not a fan of an env var fallback that silently re-enables v1. Can we make it explicit in logs/metrics when that override is used? Benji Okafor (author): Agreed. Added WARN log on startup if RBAC_V1_FALLBACK_ENABLED=true and a counter metric rbac.v1_fallback_requests_total (should stay zero). Marcus Lin (review): Risk: billing read endpoints being blocked is noisy for customers. Please include a concrete rollback instruction that on-call can execute without redeploy. Also, update the rollout plan to start with internal orgs first. Benji Okafor (author): Added runbook section with flag-first rollback: set rbacv2.enforce=false (reverts to old behavior since v1 is still compiled) OR set rbacv2.disable_v1_tranche=false (re-enables v1 checks for tranche routes) depending on failure mode. Updated rollout plan to: internal orgs -> hosted canary -> 25% -> 100%. Connor O'Brien (review): Confirmed dates: we’ll align with next Tuesday’s hosted release train. Please add a short release note for on-call and link the dashboard panel used to watch shadow-deny. Benji Okafor (author): Added internal release note + link to Grafana dashboard “RBAC v2 Migration / Shadow Deny by Route”. Amara Diallo (review): Any gateway-level v1 checks still on these routes? If yes, this might not fully remove v1. Benji Okafor (author): For this tranche, gateway auth remains tenant/project scoping only; v1 RBAC was service-side. Added a comment in the runbook noting that some routes still have gateway-level coarse checks but not RBAC role evaluation. Kaitlyn Nguyen (final): Looks good after the fallback metric/log change. Approved.
rollback_instructions: Rollback order (least disruptive first): (1) If customers see unexpected denies after enabling enforcement: flip feature flag rbacv2.enforce=false for affected org(s) (hosted) or in the deployment config (Dedicated/Private). This returns enforcement behavior to pre-v2. (2) If we need to keep v2 enforcement on globally but restore legacy v1 checks for this tranche: flip rbacv2.disable_v1_tranche=false (restores v1 middleware for the tranche routes). (3) If a binary-level issue is suspected (e.g., panic in v2 middleware): deploy previous build or revert this PR (squash revert) and re-run migration dashboards to confirm shadow-deny returns to baseline. Monitoring during rollback: watch rbac.decision_total{decision="deny"} for the tranche routes, rbac.shadow_deny_total, and rbac.v1_fallback_requests_total (should be 0 unless the emergency override is set).
release_notes: Internal: RBAC v2 migration step—legacy RBAC v1 checks disabled for initial set of control-plane read + API key endpoints once rbacv2.enforce is enabled. On-call rollback is flag-first (rbacv2.enforce / rbacv2.disable_v1_tranche).
